items.title: CogRouter: LLM Agents That Adapt Thinking Depth Per Step
items.tldr: New research introduces CogRouter, a framework that trains LLM agents to dynamically adjust their 'cognitive depth' for each step of a task, achieving SOTA performance with 62% fewer tokens by avoiding uniform over-thinking.
whyItMatters: Business impact: Drastically reduces inference cost and latency for complex, multi-step agent tasks, making them more viable for production.
Technical impact: Moves beyond fixed 'think' or 'don't think' agent patterns to a more efficient, adaptive model grounded in cognitive theory.

whatToTry.description: For complex agent workflows, prototype a simple heuristic to decide when to use a 'fast' vs. 'slow' (Chain-of-Thought) reasoning path based on step complexity, instead of always using one.
whatToTry.note: The core idea is to avoid the cost of deep reasoning on trivial steps. Start by classifying steps in your own agent's task loop.

sources.title: Think Fast and Slow: Step-Level Cognitive Depth Adaptation for LLM Agents

Technical impact: Optimizing power delivery from the grid directly to GPUs could significantly lower operational costs and enable more sustainable data center growth.

items.title: New Benchmark Exposes AI Multi-Agent Safety Gaps
items.tldr: GT-HarmBench reveals frontier AI models choose socially beneficial actions only 62% of the time in high-stakes multi-agent scenarios, highlighting critical safety gaps in coordination and conflict resolution.
whyItMatters: Business impact: Deploying AI in multi-agent environments (negotiations, markets, autonomous systems) without proper safety testing could lead to coordination failures and harmful outcomes.
Technical impact: Standard single-agent safety benchmarks miss critical multi-agent risks like Prisoner's Dilemma failures; game-theoretic interventions can improve outcomes by 18%.

whatToTry.description: Test your AI agents on GT-HarmBench scenarios (available on GitHub) to identify coordination vulnerabilities, especially if your product involves multi-agent interactions or high-stakes decision-making.
whatToTry.note: Focus on scenarios relevant to your domain from the MIT AI Risk Repository included in the benchmark.

items.title: Research: Mix vs Merge Training for Multi-Domain LLMs
items.tldr: New research finds mixing RL training across domains (coding, math, science) causes minimal interference and can create synergistic gains, challenging the need for separate training and merging.
whyItMatters: Reduces the cost and complexity of building multi-domain expert models by showing a single mixed training run can be effective.
Provides evidence that reasoning skills in one domain (e.g., math) can improve performance in another (e.g., coding), informing training strategy.

whatToTry.description: If you're fine-tuning an LLM for multiple expert tasks, consider a mixed multi-task RLHF/RLVR training run first, rather than defaulting to training separate models and merging them.
whatToTry.note: The study used open-source datasets; validate this approach on your specific domain mix and data.

items.title: Research: AI Agents + OR + Humans Best for Inventory Control

Technical impact: Demonstrates a clear 'complementarity' framework where LLMs handle context/uncertainty and OR provides theoretical grounding, challenging the 'AI vs. human' narrative.

whatToTry.description: If you're building for operations/logistics, prototype a decision pipeline where an LLM agent analyzes contextual signals (e.g., news, weather) to adjust the parameters of a traditional inventory algorithm, rather than replacing it.

items.title: New Research: Entity State Tuning for Better Temporal Knowledge Graphs
items.tldr: Researchers propose Entity State Tuning (EST), a framework that gives AI models persistent memory for temporal knowledge graphs, solving 'episodic amnesia' and improving long-term forecasting accuracy.
whyItMatters: Enables AI systems to maintain coherent memory over time, crucial for applications like supply chain forecasting or customer journey modeling.
Provides a plug-and-play framework to upgrade existing sequence models with persistent state, improving performance without full retraining.

whatToTry.description: Review the open-source code to see if EST's 'global state buffer' concept could be adapted to give your product's AI features a better long-term memory, especially if you work with time-series or sequential user data.
whatToTry.note: The framework is encoder-agnostic, meaning it could potentially be tested with various model backbones you might already be using.
